news.title: Challenger Series Preview: A Four-Round Dash to Glory Across the Globe
news.standfirst: With two multi-class categories, four distinct world-class venues, and a drop-week rule, the stage is set for a thrilling new Race Club campaign.
news.body:
## A Four-Stage Gauntlet Across Global Motorsport

The engines are about to ignite for a fresh season of Race Club competition as the Challenger Series opens its doors to drivers ready to tackle multi-class racing at its absolute limits. Blending the sheer aerodynamic speed of the Hypercar class with the door-to-door intensity of LMGT3, this four-round campaign is designed to test every facet of driver skill, traffic management, and championship strategy. With points scaled to race duration and a mandatory drop week in play, every single lap will carry enormous weight from the opening green flag to the final checkered light at Le Mans.

The tour kicks off in California at the legendary Laguna Seca circuit for the 45-minute Prologue. Drivers will instantly face the daunting plunge through the Corkscrew, where millimetric precision is required to keep a Hypercar on the tarmac or defend a tight line in LMGT3. From North America, the championship crosses the Atlantic to Portugal for the Roar in the Algarve at Portimão. This 60-minute Medium race presents a sweeping rollercoaster of blind crests and technical elevation changes, demanding peak focus over an extended stint. Round 3 brings the paddock back to the United States for the 45-minute Sunset Sprint at Sebring, where punishing concrete bumps and low evening light will test driver resilience in a race into dusk. Finally, the season reaches its climax at Circuit de la Sarthe for The Ultimate Finale, a 72-minute endurance showdown where high-stakes points can dramatically tilt the final standings.

## Hypercars and GT3s Ready for Battle

The grid for the Challenger Series showcases a magnificent array of machinery across both classes. In the top-tier Hypercar category, lightweight engineering meets hybrid power. Grid entries feature iconic prototypes including the Ferrari 499P, the Toyota TR010, the screaming V12-powered Aston Martin Valkyrie, and the thunderous Cadillac V-Series.R. Complemented by the aggressive BMW M Hybrid V8, the striking Alpine A424, the sleek Genesis GMR-001, and the wingless Peugeot 9X8, the prototype field promises breath-taking top speeds and intense battles for outright honors.

Equally compelling is the LMGT3 roster, where production-based grand tourers fight in close quarters. Heavyweights such as the Porsche 911 GT3 R (Type 992), Ferrari 296 GT3 Evo, and Aston Martin Vantage AMR GT3 lead a stacked lineup that includes the roaring Ford Mustang GT3, the nimble McLaren 720S GT3 Evo, the muscle-bound Corvette Z06 GT3.R, the proven Mercedes-AMG GT3, the razor-sharp Lexus RC F GT3, and the formidable BMW M4 GT3. Managing traffic between the high-downforce prototypes and the balanced GT3 machines will be the true hallmark of any driver aiming for class victory.

## High-Stakes Points and Strategic Depth

The championship architecture adds a compelling tactical layer to every stint. Points are awarded based on race length, meaning the 45-minute sprint rounds at Laguna Seca and Sebring yield 25 points for a win, while the 60-minute clash at Portimão elevates victory to 38 points. The crown jewel finale at Le Mans offers a massive 50 points to the winner, ensuring that title fights remain alive until the very end. Crucially, bonus points are available in every race: single points awarded for qualifying on pole position, setting the race's fastest lap, and leading the highest number of laps.

Adding another wrinkle to the championship math is the single drop-week rule, which allows drivers to discard their worst result of the four rounds. This safety net gives competitors room to recover from an unlucky incident or a missed round, but it also means that consistent front-runners must constantly calculate their net points position. Seats across both classes remain open as registration stays live, inviting racers of all experience levels to claim their spot on the starting grid, master the traffic, and chase glory in the Challenger Series.
